[[File:Julio Cesar Firrufino.png|thumb|Front page of ''Platica'' (1626)]]
'''Julio Cesar Firrufino''' or '''Ferrufino''' (16th century) was an [[engineer]] and [[mathematician]] who had a chair in mathematics in [[Madrid]] from 1604 to 1650.

== Life and work ==
He was the son of Julian Firrufino (ca 1535–1604), born in [[Alessandria]] ([[Duchy of Milan]]) who had also a chair in Geometry and Artillery granted by the king of Spain.<ref>{{smallcaps|Vicente Maroto}}, page 8.</ref> However, we know few biographical data of Julio Cesar, his son.<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, page 172.</ref> Only from a document dated 1644, we know he was 66 years old, so we can suppose he was born in 1578, when his father had a chair of Naval Artillery in the ''[[Casa de Contratación]]'' and, probably, he was born in [[Sevilla]].<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, page 174.</ref>

In 1600 he was assistant of the Spanish minister of Artillery<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, page 175.</ref> and from 1604, after the death of his father, he was appointed to a chair on Mathematics and Fortification,<ref>It is not clear in which academic institution, see {{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, pages 177–178.</ref> after the approval of [[:es:Andrés García de Céspedes|Andrés García de Céspedes]] and [[:ca:João Baptista Lavanha|João Baptista Lavanha]] who examined him.<ref>{{smallcaps|Capel, Sánchez & Moncada}}, page 99.</ref> He was in charge of the chair until 1650, one year before his death; in this date he was replaced by his student [[Luis Carduchi]], member of a family of old friends of Firrufino.<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, pages 179–180.</ref>

In 1626 he published ''Plática Manual y Breve Compendio de Artillería'', which was an abstract of a treatise of artillery that he was not allowed to publish by political reasons.<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, pages 181–182.</ref>

In 1638 he was accused by fraud in the production of 66 artillery guns in Sevilla; for this reason he was imprisoned during some time in 1644.<ref>{{smallcaps|Díaz Moreno}}, pages 183 i ss.</ref>

In 1648 was published his most important work: ''El perfecto artillero'', which is an encyclopedic treatise, but not much original, based in [[Niccolò Fontana Tartaglia|Tartaglia]] ideas.<ref>{{smallcaps|Navarro Loidi}}, page 596.</ref>
